title_he: מַה־יָּפֶה כִּי נִקָּהֵל סָבִיב לַיָּדִיד לְהַלֵּל
review: 3:1–3:4 repeats 'This is the Father's joy, that' twice, with the second clause changed (we seek His glory / we see Jesus alone). The Hebrew keeps the anaphora שְׂשׂוֹן הָאָב כִּי at both 3:1 and 3:3, as the Arabic does, because the doubling is what turns the stanza from duty into the Father's own delight.

5:1–5:2 הוּא יְדִידֵנוּ הֶעָשִׁיר … נֶעֱשַׁרְנוּ — 2 Cor 8:9 (כִּי בִגְלַל עֲנִיּוּתוֹ תַּעֲשִׁירוּ); the Arabic فَهُوَ حَبِيبُنَا الْغَنِيّ / وَمِنْ غِنَاهُ نَغْتَنِي is that exchange, and the Hebrew keeps הֶעָשִׁיר / נֶעֱשַׁרְנוּ as the same root, so the riches are transferred, not merely admired.

4:1–4:2 בֵּין אָהוּבִים יִשְׁכֹּן … יְצַוֶּה — the Arabic وَسْطَ الْأَحِبَّا يَحْضُرُ / بِالْبَرَكَاتِ يَأْمُرُ is 'among the loved ones He is present, commanding blessings'; the Hebrew keeps the promised presence 'in the midst' (Exod 20:24, בְּכָל־הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר אַזְכִּיר אֶת־שְׁמִי) and the verb 'command' for the blessing.

1:1–1:2 כָּבוֹד לְמִי שֶׁהִשְׁפִּיל … לְהָאִיר — the Arabic مَجْدًا لِمَنْ تَنَازَلَ حَتَّى يُنِيرَ is 'glory to Him who condescended so as to enlighten'; the Hebrew keeps the purpose clause with לְהָאִיר, so the condescension is not merely admired but names its end.

1:4 יוֹשֵׁב מְרוֹמִים — the Arabic سَاكِنِ الْعُلَا is 'Dweller of the heights'; the Hebrew uses יֹשֵׁב מָרוֹם, the Isaiah title (Isa 33:5, יֹשֵׁב מָרוֹם), kept so the stanza's arc runs from the lowly assembly to the exalted throne.
